notes.text: I perceive of a truth — More clearly than ever, from such a concurrence of circumstances. That God is not a respecter of persons - Is not partial in his love. The words mean, in a particular sense, that he does not confine his love to one nation; in a general, that he is loving to every man, and willeth all men should be saved.

But in every nation he that feareth God and worketh righteousness — He that, first, reverences God, as great, wise, good, the cause, end, and governor of all things; and secondly, from this awful regard to him, not only avoids all known evil, but endeavours, according to the best light he has, to do all things well; is accepted of him - Through Christ, though he knows him not. The assertion is express, and admits of no exception. He is in the favour of God, whether enjoying his written word and ordinances or not. Nevertheless the addition of these is an unspeakable blessing to those who were before in some measure accepted. Otherwise God would never have sent an angel from heaven to direct Cornelius to St. Peter.

This is the word which God sent — When he sent his Son into the world, preaching - Proclaiming by him-peace between God and man, whether Jew or Gentile, by the God-man. He is Lord of both; yea, Lord of and over all.

Ye know the word which was published — You know the facts in general, the meaning of which I shall now more particularly explain and confirm to you. The baptism which John preached - To which he invited them by his preaching, in token of their repentance. This began in Galilee, which is near Cesarea.

How God anointed Jesus — Particularly at his baptism, thereby inaugurating him to his office: with the Holy Ghost and with power - It is worthy our remark, that frequently when the Holy Ghost is mentioned there is added a word particularly adapted to the present circumstance. So the deacons were to be full of the Holy Ghost and wisdom, chap. vi, 3. Barnabas was full of the Holy Ghost and faith, chap. xi, 24. The disciples were filled with joy, and with the Holy Ghost, chap. xiii, 52. And here, where his mighty works are mentioned, Christ himself is said to be anointed with the Holy Ghost and with power. For God was with him-He speaks sparingly here of the majesty of Christ, as considering the state of his hearers.
Not now to all the people — As before his death; to us who did eat and drink with him - That is, conversed familiarly and continually with him, in the time of his ministry.

It is he who is ordained by God the Judge of the living and the dead — Of all men, whether they are alive at his coming, or had died before it. This was declaring to them, in the strongest terms, how entirely their happiness depended on a timely and humble subjection to him who was to be their final Judge.

To him give all the prophets witness — Speaking to heathens he does not quote any in particular; that every one who believeth in him - Whether he be Jew or Gentile; receiveth remission of sins - Though he had not before either feared God, or worked righteousness.

glossa.text: *He is not a respecter of persons,* etc. ((BEDA.)) It is plain that God is not a respecter of persons, etc., *as far as* but that they should receive all that believe.

*You know,* etc. ((RAB.)) It is to be read thus: You know Jesus as John preached him: Jesus of Nazareth, how he anointed him, etc. Or: this John preached, that he anointed him, not indeed after an earthly manner, but by the spirit and the power of signs.

*Who went about,* etc. In the Greek is added, *through forty days,* not that they ate and drank with him daily, for it would be contrary to John, who interposes eight days in which he was not seen by them, that he might be made manifest the third time, and for as many days he fasted before his death, being in need of food, whereas he ate after the resurrection being now not in need of food. He fasted before his death, that we might abstain from the desires of this world. He ate, teaching by this that he is with us until the consummation of the world. Fasting is in the contest, because he who is in the struggle abstains from all things. Food is in the hope of peace, which shall be perfect, when this mortal shall have put on immortality. But we, while we take the way of the Lord, fast from the vanity of the world, and are refreshed by the promise to come.

((RAB.)) Through forty days, not continually, but at certain turns taken within that quadragenary number of days.

*And we drank. ((BEDA.))* Here Peter sets forth what is passed over in silence in the Gospel, that after the resurrection he drank with Christ, unless perhaps we believe it to be indicated there, where he says: *Until I drink it with you in the kingdom of my Father ((Matth. XXVI))*.

notes.text: Salvation — My saviour.
Doth valiantly — These are the words of that song of praise now mentioned.
Exalted — Hath appeared evidently, and wrought powerfully and gloriously.
Open — O ye porters, appointed by God for this work. The gates - Of the Lord's tabernacle: where the rule of righteousness was kept and taught, and the sacrifices of righteousness were offered.

The righteous — As David was a type of Christ and the temple of heaven, so this place hath a farther prospect than David, and relates to Christ's ascending into heaven, and opening the gates of that blessed temple, both for himself and for all believers.

The builders — The commonwealth of Israel and the church of God are here and elsewhere compared to a building, wherein, as the people are the stones, so the princes and rulers are the builders. And as these master-builders rejected David, so their successors rejected Christ. Head stone - The chief stone in the whole building, by which the several parts of the building are upheld and firmly united together. Thus David united all the tribes and families of Israel: and thus Christ united Jews and Gentiles together. And therefore this place is justly expounded of Christ, Mark xii, 10 Acts iv, 11 Rom. ix, 32 Eph. ii, 20. And to him the words agree more properly than to David.
Made — Or sanctified as a season never to be forgotten.

glossa.text:
*Let him now say.* ((ID.)) As I admonish you, so do you admonish one another; or, *let him say,* that is, let him confess.

*Because for ever.* Behold four verses of one ending.
*He is become my salvation.* ((ID.)) He is not made what he was not to himself; but he is salvation to them converted, which he was not to them turned away.
*I shall not die.* ((ID.)) The Church says it, since the persecutor thinks that by a slaughter of funerals he can blot out the Christian name, whereas he rather increases it.

*Chastising.* ((CASS.)) But why he bore so many things, he shows: *Chastising,* whatever they do is the chastisement of the Lord. Let them claim nothing to themselves; he is not given over to death whose vices are purged. ((AUG.)) Often a father amends his sons by worthless servants, when for those he prepares punishment, for these an inheritance. And what the inheritance is may be known from this: *Open ye the gates.* What within? *Having entered I will confess.*

*Open ye.* ((CASS.)) In the third place he desires that the gates of Jerusalem be opened to him, where he speaks also of the corner stone. Open, O prophets, who bear the keys of the kingdom of heaven. *The gates.* ((CASS., HIER.)) They who have entered through these gates of doctrine praise truly; outside the Catholic Church there is no praise of God. ((CASS.)) All these gates lead to one, which is Christ, through whom the just enter into heaven; whence: *I am the door, through which if any man enter in, he shall be safe ((Joan. X))* . And elsewhere: *No man cometh to the Father, but by me ((Joan. XIV))*. ((AUG.)) Behold, he has made mention of both worlds: and because this gate has appeared as Christ, *I will confess to thee,* giving thanks with gladness, *because thou hast heard* at the coming of the Son; for the just of former times were asking for the coming. *The gates of justice.* That is, the gates of death, etc., *as far as* that is, through it unto life.
*They that build.* ((ID.)) The Jews alone, worshipping God, were building, the rest being destroyed through idolatry; but they did not finish, because they despised Christ.
*This is done by the Lord.* Or, *This is done by the Lord for him,* according to another reading. ((ID.)) That is, unto the honour of the Father.

*This is the day.* This is the jubilee year, figuratively observed under the law, which is called *remitting,* or *beginning,* because then bondmen were set free, possessions were restored to their owners: and we on this day have been redeemed from the servitude of sin, to whom an eternal inheritance has been restored. ((CASS.)) *This is the day.* Although he made all days, this one singularly, on which the Lord came, on which it is fitting to rejoice, because the devil lost his right and man lived again; and because this is so,

notes.text: Ye are saved, if ye hold fast — Your salvation is begun, and will be perfected, if ye continue in the faith. Unless ye have believed in vain - Unless indeed your faith was only a delusion.
I received — From Christ himself. It was not a fiction of my own. Isaiah liii, 8, 9.
According to the scriptures — He proves it first from scripture, then from the testimony of a cloud of witnesses. Psalm xvi, 10.
By the twelve — This was their standing appellation; but their full number was not then present.
Above five hundred — Probably in Galilee. A glorious and incontestable proof! The greater part remain - Alive.

Then by all the apostles — The twelve were mentioned ver. 5. This title here, therefore, seems to include the seventy; if not all those, likewise, whom God afterwards sent to plant the gospel in heathen nations.

An untimely birth — It was impossible to abase himself more than he does by this single appellation. As an abortion is not worthy the name of a man, so he affirms himself to be not worthy the name of an apostle.
I persecuted the church — True believers are humbled all their lives, even for the sins they committed before they believed.

I laboured more than they all — That is, more than any of them, from a deep sense of the peculiar love God had shown me. Yet, to speak more properly, it is not I, but the grace of God that is with me - This it is which at first qualified me for the work, and still excites me to zeal and diligence in it.
Whether I or they, so we preach — All of us speak the same thing.

glossa.text: *By which also you are saved.* If you hold fast that Gospel, that is, the resurrection of the dead, on the ground on which I confirmed it to you, that is, by the resurrection of Christ. *Unless you have believed in vain.* Which is, if you do not hold the resurrection of the dead. That faith is empty which is not received under the hope of resurrection.

*He rose again the third day.* And this I said according to the Scriptures. For Osee says: *After two days he will quicken us, and on the third day we shall rise again in his sight ((Ose. VI))*. If he who was dead and buried rose again, doubt not that the dead and the buried shall rise again.
*He was seen by Cephas.* Before the other men to whom he is read to have appeared in the Gospel, otherwise it would be contrary to that which is read, that he appeared first to the women.

*As one born out of due time.* He is called one born out of due time because he was born outside the lawful season, that is, before he ought, or because, born again later and more tardily, he received the apostolate when Christ had already been taken up. Or, like one born out of due time, because I am the least, whether in time and calling, not in dignity, in labour, or in preaching. This he said truly, for humility's sake, and he proves it, saying: *I am not worthy.* Why then an Apostle? *But by the grace of God* At the first, grace alone, since no merits went before save evil ones. But afterwards, through grace, merits begin.

*More abundantly.* This was the more fulfilled, because he lived by the work of his hands, and did no less for the Gospel. And lest the will without the grace of God should be thought able to do anything, he adds: *Not I, but the grace,* etc
*And so you believed.* He reproves them: because, though this faith was manifest among all the churches, they nevertheless had fallen away from it.

notes.text: Matt. xxviii, 1; Mark xvi, 1; Luke xxiv, 1.
Peter went out — Of the city.
Peter seeth the linen clothes lie — and the napkin folded up - The angels who ministered to him when he rose, undoubtedly folded up the napkin and linen clothes.
He saw — That the body was not there, and believed - That they had taken it away as Mary said.
For as yet — They had no thought of his rising again.
They went home — Not seeing what they could do farther.
But Mary stood — With more constancy. Mark xvi, 9.
Jesus saith to her, Mary — With his usual voice and accent.

Touch me not — Or rather, Do not cling to me (for she held him by the feet,) Matt. xxviii, 9. Detain me not now. You will have other opportunities of conversing with me. For I am not ascended to my Father - I have not yet left the world. But go immediately to my brethren -- thus does he intimate in the strongest manner the forgiveness of their fault, even without ever mentioning it. These exquisite touches, which everywhere abound in the evangelical writings, show how perfectly Christ knew our frame. I ascend - He anticipates it in his thoughts, and so speaks of it as a thing already present. To my Father and your Father, to my God and your God - This uncommon expression shows that the only- begotten Son has all kind of fellowship with God. And a fellowship with God the Father, some way resembling his own, he bestows upon his brethren. Yet he does not say, Our God: for no creature can be raised to an equality with him: but my God and your God: intimating that the Father is his in a singular and incommunicable manner; and ours through him, in such a kind as a creature is capable of.

glossa.text: *And they ran.* John signifies the Synagogue, which came first to the tomb but did not enter, because she heard the prophecies concerning the incarnation and the passion, but refused to believe him even dead. Peter signifies the Church, which knew him dead in the flesh and believed him living God; after whom she too, in Judaea, will enter at the end.

*It is separated.* Because the sacraments of the Godhead are incomprehensible and set far from the knowledge of our weakness. In a thing wrapped up, neither end nor beginning is seen. So the loftiness of the Godhead neither began to be, nor ceases. *Into one place.* Because God is not in the sundering of minds, but in unity. Or, the napkin of the head is the passion of Christ, whose sacraments are hidden apart from unbelievers, because it is far from ours, because he suffered willingly and without fault, we unwillingly and with fault.
*For as yet.* That is, to such a degree that, although it was openly said by the Lord himself, because of their custom of hearing parables from him, they did not understand.

*Weeping.* She now weeps more for him taken away than for him slain, because of so great a master, whose life had been taken from her, not even the memory remained, and this grief held her there. *While therefore,* etc. Although she knew that he was not there, yet because she grieves too much, she gave no thought either to her own eyes or to the eyes of those two who believed. Or rather this was done by divine prompting.

*She saw two.* The angels, that is, messengers, signify that the Gospel of Christ is to be announced from the head even to the feet, that is, from the beginning even to the end. And he was to be announced from his passion, because he is God before the ages, and man at the end of the age. The angel therefore sits at the head when he says: *In the beginning was the Word.* At the feet, when he says: *The Word was made flesh.* Or the two angels are the two Testaments, the one former, the other following. Joined together, while with equal sense they announce him incarnate, dead, raised again.

*Why weepest thou?* As if he should say: *Sin not* *peccare*; read *plorare*, "Do not weep" -- the next sentence says what is forbidden is her tears. They forbid her tears, in a manner announcing joy. But she, thinking that they asked as not knowing, brings forth the cause of her tears: *Because they have taken away my Lord,* that is, the body of my Lord.
*And she knew not that it was Jesus,* etc. Because she had her back toward him whom she believed not to have risen; because she loved and doubted, she saw and did not know him.

*Whom seekest thou? She, thinking that it was the gardener, saith to him.* Not that he doubted whom she was seeking, but because she knows not whom she seeks; for she seeks not Christ, but him whom she thinks carried off. *Lord.* Him whom she thinks a gardener she calls Lord, that she might honour the man of whom she was asking a kindness. Nor does she call him Lord in the same way as she calls him whom she seeks as taken away. But recognizing Jesus she calls him master, because she calls to mind him from whom she was learning to distinguish things human and divine. *If thou hast taken him away.* She does not say whom, because the force of love works this in the mind, that of him whom she always thinks she believes no other to be ignorant.

*Mary. She turning saith to him: Rabboni, which is to say master. Jesus saith to her.* After he had called her by the common name, and was not recognized, he calls her by her name, as if he should say, Know again him by whom thou art known again.

*Mary of Magdalene came announcing to the disciples that she had seen the Lord,* etc. There the fault is cut off *undet* it proceeded. A woman gave death to a man to drink; now a woman announces life to men; and she who then [told] the words of the serpent now relates the words of the Life-giver; as if God should say by the very facts: From what hand the draught of death was brought in, from that same hand receive ye the draught of life.

hymns.title: The strife is o'er, the battle done
Almighty God, through Jesus Christ you overcame death
I come to the garden alone
To God be the glory, great things he hath done

praise.title: Yet Not I But Through Christ in Me

echoes.text: For Yahweh your God, he is God of gods, and Lord of lords, the great God, the mighty, and the awesome, who doesn’t respect persons, nor takes reward.
echoes.note: 'God doesn't show favoritism' (ou prosopolemptes) directly restates the Deuteronomic confession that God 'regards not persons (does not lift the face) nor takes a bribe.' Distinctive theological formula; the basis for the whole Gentile-inclusion argument. High volume and coherence.

echoes.text: How beautiful on the mountains are the feet of him who brings good news, who publishes peace, who brings good news of good, who publishes salvation, who says to Zion, “Your God reigns!”
echoes.note: 'Preaching good news of peace' (euangelizomenos eirenen) reproduces the herald who 'publishes peace, brings good tidings' on the mountains. The gospel-of-peace formula in v36 is drawn from this servant-song herald text. High volume.

echoes.text: The Spirit of the Lord Yahweh is on me; because Yahweh has anointed me to preach good news to the humble. He has sent me to bind up the broken hearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and release to those who are bound;
echoes.note: 'God anointed him with the Holy Spirit and with power, who went about doing good' reflects 'the Spirit of the Lord GOD is upon me, because the LORD has anointed me' to bring good news and release. The Spirit-anointing summary of Jesus' ministry draws on this servant text. High coherence.
echoes.lxxText: The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has anointed me; he has sent me to preach glad tidings to the poor, to heal the broken in heart, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and recovery of sight to the blind;

echoes.text: If a man has committed a sin worthy of death, and he is put to death, and you hang him on a tree; his body shall not remain all night on the tree, but you shall surely bury him the same day; for he who is hanged is accursed of God; that you don’t defile your land which Yahweh your God gives you for an inheritance.
echoes.note: 'Whom they also killed, hanging him on a tree' (kremasantes epi xylou) deliberately invokes the law that a man 'hanged on a tree' is accursed of God and must be taken down. The xylon language is the distinctive Deuteronomic marker. High volume.

echoes.text: Now therefore let the fear of Yahweh be on you. Take heed and do it: for there is no iniquity with Yahweh our God, nor respect of persons, nor taking of bribes.”
echoes.note: Jehoshaphat's charge that 'with the LORD our God there is no iniquity, nor respect of persons, nor taking of gifts' is a second locus of the 'no partiality' formula informing v34. Recurrence strengthens the allusion.

echoes.text: I create the fruit of the lips: Peace, peace, to him who is far off and to him who is near,” says Yahweh; “and I will heal them.”
echoes.note: 'Peace, peace, to him that is far off, and to him that is near' undergirds the proclamation of peace now extended to the far-off Gentiles in Cornelius's house; coherent with the chapter's inclusion theme.

echoes.text: “Behold, my servant, whom I uphold; my chosen, in whom my soul delights— I have put my Spirit on him. He will bring justice to the nations.
echoes.note: 'My chosen, in whom my soul delights; I have put my Spirit upon him' supports v38's portrait of the Spirit-endowed servant and v41's 'witnesses chosen before by God.' Thematic coherence high; verbal moderate.

echoes.text: After two days he will revive us. On the third day he will raise us up, and we will live before him.
echoes.note: 'God raised him up the third day' resonates with 'on the third day he will raise us up, that we may live before him.' A recurrent NT third-day intertext; figural/typological with moderate verbal touch.

echoes.text: and they shall teach no more every man his neighbor, and every man his brother, saying, Know Yahweh; for they shall all know me, from their least to their greatest, says Yahweh: for I will forgive their iniquity, and their sin will I remember no more.
echoes.note: 'Everyone who believes in him will receive remission of sins' to which 'all the prophets testify' echoes the new-covenant promise 'I will forgive their iniquity, and remember their sin no more,' the prophetic witness to forgiveness Peter invokes. Coherent.

echoes.text: Behold, on the mountains the feet of him who brings good news, who publishes peace! Keep your feasts, Judah! Perform your vows, for the wicked one will no more pass through you. He is utterly cut off.
echoes.note: 'Behold upon the mountains the feet of him that brings good tidings, that publishes peace' is a parallel herald-of-peace text reinforcing the Isaianic background of v36.

echoes.text: He sends his word, and heals them, and delivers them from their graves.
echoes.note: 'The word which he sent to the children of Israel' faintly echoes 'he sent his word and healed them,' apt given the immediate reference to Jesus 'healing all who were oppressed.' Low volume.

echoes.text: Be it far from you to do things like that, to kill the righteous with the wicked, so that the righteous should be like the wicked. May that be far from you. Shouldn’t the Judge of all the earth do right?”
echoes.note: Jesus 'appointed by God as the Judge of the living and the dead' echoes the title 'Judge of all the earth.' Thematic.

echoes.text: Let them sing before Yahweh, for he comes to judge the earth. He will judge the world with righteousness, and the peoples with equity.
echoes.note: 'He comes to judge the earth... the world with righteousness, and the peoples with equity' undergirds the designation of the risen one as eschatological Judge in v42.

echoes.text: The inhabitant won’t say, “I am sick.” The people who dwell therein will be forgiven their iniquity.
echoes.note: 'The people that dwell therein shall be forgiven their iniquity' is among the prophetic texts of forgiveness that 'all the prophets testify' to in v43. Faint, offered maximally.

spans.label: Tarsus & Antioch
spans.note: Sent home to Tarsus, then fetched by Barnabas to teach at Antioch, where the disciples were first called Christians. Ends with the famine-relief visit to Jerusalem.

places.name: Jerusalem
places.id: The City of David and Old City, on the spurs above the Kidron Valley, c. 50 km from the Mediterranean. Pre-Israelite Jebus; named here as the seat of Adoni-Zedek, leader of the southern coalition.

places.name: Judea
places.id: The Roman administrative province (later procuratorial province) covering the southern hill country of Israel — Jerusalem, the Judean wilderness, and territory south to the Negev. The Greco-Roman successor to the Hasmonean and Herodian Iudaea. Pin sits in the central hill country.

places.name: Galilee
places.id: The northern region of Roman-period Palestine, bounded by the Jezreel valley (south), the Lebanese mountains (north), the Mediterranean (west), and the Jordan / Sea of Galilee (east). Subdivided into Lower Galilee (the Jesus traditions are mostly here) and Upper Galilee.

places.name: Nazareth
places.id: Modern en-Nasira / Nazareth in Lower Galilee, c. 30 km west of the Sea of Galilee. A village of perhaps 200-400 in the early first century, identified through continuous habitation, tomb evidence, and the third-century Caesarea inscription naming it as a priestly course settlement.

echoes.attribution: Catena, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wilson Pruitt / Wroot Press)

echoes.text: But he was pierced for our transgressions. He was crushed for our iniquities. The punishment that brought our peace was on him; and by his wounds we are healed. All we like sheep have gone astray. Everyone has turned to his own way; and Yahweh has laid on him the iniquity of us all.
echoes.note: Paul's creedal 'Christ died for our sins according to the Scriptures' (v.3) draws on the Servant who is 'wounded for our transgressions' and on whom the LORD lays 'the iniquity of us all.' Volume is moderate (no verbatim quotation) but coherence is high: the vicarious sin-bearing death is the only OT text supplying the formula, and Isaiah 53 was a primary resurrection-era proof-text. Availability is secure.

echoes.text: He was taken away by oppression and judgment; and as for his generation, who considered that he was cut off out of the land of the living and stricken for the disobedience of my people? They made his grave with the wicked, and with a rich man in his death; although he had done no violence, neither was any deceit in his mouth. Yet it pleased Yahweh to bruise him. He has caused him to suffer. When you make his soul an offering for sin, he shall see his […]
echoes.note: The Servant 'cut off out of the land of the living,' 'numbered with the transgressors,' who 'bore the sin of many,' and is afterward vindicated ('he shall see... he shall prolong his days') undergirds the death-burial-vindication shape of the kerygma in vv.3-5. Recurrence: Paul appeals to Isaiah 53 elsewhere (Rom 4:25; 10:16). The 'according to the Scriptures' refrain points here for the death.

echoes.text: After two days he will revive us. On the third day he will raise us up, and we will live before him.
echoes.note: 'After two days he will revive us; on the third day he will raise us up' is the strongest single OT candidate for 'raised on the third day according to the Scriptures' (v.4), since no other text gives a third-day resurrection. Targumic/rabbinic tradition read Hosea 6:2 of resurrection, supporting availability. Contested because Paul never cites it explicitly and the LXX wording differs.

echoes.text: For you will not leave my soul in Sheol, neither will you allow your holy one to see corruption.
echoes.note: 'You will not abandon my soul to Sheol, nor let your holy one see corruption' was the apostolic resurrection proof-text (Acts 2:27; 13:35) and plausibly stands behind 'raised on the third day according to the Scriptures.' Coherence with the burial-then-raising sequence (vv.4) is good; volume is low here since Paul does not quote it. Marked echo, not quotation.

echoes.text: Yahweh prepared a great fish to swallow up Jonah, and Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights.
echoes.note: 'Three days and three nights in the belly of the fish' is a possible scriptural warrant for the third-day timing, read figurally of death and deliverance (cf. Matt 12:40). Volume and recurrence in Paul are nil, so this is a faint, contested figural reading offered only because the 'according to the Scriptures' for the third day demands OT grounding.

echoes.attribution: Catena, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wilson Pruitt / Wroot Press)

echoes.text: In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth. The earth was formless and empty. Darkness was on the surface of the deep and God’s Spirit was hovering over the surface of the waters. God said, “Let there be light,” and there was light. God saw the light, and saw that it was good. God divided the light from the darkness. God called the light “day”, and the darkness he called “night”. There was evening and there was morning, the first day.
echoes.note: The resurrection occurs on 'the first day of the week' 'while it was still dark,' deliberately echoing the first day of creation when light dawns over darkness (Gen 1:3-5). John, who opened his Gospel 'In the beginning' (Jn 1:1 = Gen 1:1), frames the resurrection as inaugurated new creation; high Coherence with the Gospel's creation Christology and strong Volume in the temporal marker.

echoes.text: Yahweh God planted a garden eastward, in Eden, and there he put the man whom he had formed. Out of the ground Yahweh God made every tree to grow that is pleasant to the sight, and good for food, including the tree of life in the middle of the garden and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil. A river went out of Eden to water the garden; and from there it was parted, and became the source of four rivers. The name of the first is Pishon: it flows […]
echoes.note: The tomb is in a garden (Jn 19:41), and the empty-tomb scene is staged there, recalling Eden where God placed the man (Gen 2:8,15). The garden setting binds the whole pericope to a new-Adam/new-creation typology that surfaces explicitly when Mary mistakes Jesus for the gardener (20:15).

echoes.text: By night on my bed, I sought him whom my soul loves. I sought him, but I didn’t find him. I will get up now, and go about the city; in the streets and in the squares I will seek him whom my soul loves. I sought him, but I didn’t find him. The watchmen who go about the city found me; “Have you seen him whom my soul loves?” I had scarcely passed from them, when I found him whom my soul loves. I held him, and would not let him go, until I had brought him […]
echoes.note: Mary comes seeking 'the Lord' in the dark and finds the place empty, mirroring the bride who 'on my bed by night sought him whom my soul loves; I sought him, but found him not.' The Song's seeking-not-finding-then-finding pattern unfolds across 20:1-16; medium Volume but strong Coherence given Jewish nuptial readings of the Song available in the Second-Temple period.

echoes.text: For you will not leave my soul in Sheol, neither will you allow your holy one to see corruption.
echoes.note: The narrator notes 'they didn't know the Scripture, that he must rise from the dead' (20:9); the OT warrant most plausibly in view is 'you will not abandon my soul to Sheol, nor allow your holy one to see corruption,' the standard apostolic resurrection proof-text. The reference is generic ('the Scripture') so the source is reconstructed from early Christian usage.

echoes.text: After two days he will revive us. On the third day he will raise us up, and we will live before him.
echoes.note: The third-day raising ('after two days he will revive us; on the third day he will raise us up') is a candidate background for the conviction that Jesus 'must rise.' Faint and contested: John never cites Hosea, and the day-count is implicit, lowering Volume.

echoes.text: You shall make two cherubim of hammered gold. You shall make them at the two ends of the mercy seat. Make one cherub at the one end, and one cherub at the other end. You shall make the cherubim on its two ends of one piece with the mercy seat. The cherubim shall spread out their wings upward, covering the mercy seat with their wings, with their faces toward one another. The faces of the cherubim shall be toward the mercy seat. You shall put the mercy seat […]
echoes.note: Mary sees 'two angels in white sitting, one at the head, and one at the feet, where the body of Jesus had lain' — a striking image of the two cherubim of beaten gold facing each other over the mercy seat of the ark, between whom God's presence dwelt. The empty slab framed by two angels figures the tomb as the new holy of holies; high Coherence with Johannine temple typology.

echoes.text: I lifted up my eyes, and looked, and behold, a man clothed in linen, whose thighs were adorned with pure gold of Uphaz: his body also was like the beryl, and his face as the appearance of lightning, and his eyes as flaming torches, and his arms and his feet like burnished brass, and the voice of his words like the voice of a multitude.
echoes.note: The dazzling angelic figures 'in white' draw on the Danielic vision of the man clothed in linen with a face like lightning. Volume is modest since John specifies only white garments, but the radiant-angel topos is widely available in apocalyptic.

echoes.text: I opened to my beloved; but my beloved left; and had gone away. My heart went out when he spoke. I looked for him, but I didn’t find him. I called him, but he didn’t answer. The watchmen who go about the city found me. They beat me. They bruised me. The keepers of the walls took my cloak away from me. I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem, If you find my beloved, that you tell him that I am faint with love. Friends
echoes.note: Mary's lament 'they have taken away my Lord, and I don't know where they have laid him' continues the bride-seeking-her-beloved pattern of the Song (5:6 'I sought him, but I could not find him'). Reinforces the 20:1 allusion through Recurrence within the same scene.

echoes.text: Yahweh God planted a garden eastward, in Eden, and there he put the man whom he had formed. Out of the ground Yahweh God made every tree to grow that is pleasant to the sight, and good for food, including the tree of life in the middle of the garden and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil. A river went out of Eden to water the garden; and from there it was parted, and became the source of four rivers. The name of the first is Pishon: it flows […]
echoes.note: Mary supposes the risen Jesus to be 'the gardener' in the garden of the tomb — John's deliberate irony casting Jesus as the new Adam who tends the garden (Gen 2:15), undoing Eden's loss. The garden + gardener convergence raises Volume and Coherence above the faint garden echo of 20:1.

echoes.text: I had scarcely passed from them, when I found him whom my soul loves. I held him, and would not let him go, until I had brought him into my mother’s house, into the room of her who conceived me.
echoes.note: 'Scarcely had I passed them when I found him whom my soul loves. I held him, and would not let him go' lies behind Mary's recognition and Jesus' 'Don't hold me' (20:16-17). The seeking-then-clinging sequence completes the Canticle pattern begun at 20:1; medium confidence on the cumulative force of the recurrence.

echoes.text: I will declare your name to my brothers. In the midst of the assembly, I will praise you.
echoes.note: 'Go to my brothers' (20:17) recalls the vindicated sufferer's vow 'I will declare your name to my brothers,' the turn from passion to proclamation in the psalm John has quoted at the cross (19:24). The Psalm 22 frame gives 'my brothers' high Coherence and Recurrence within the Johannine passion.

echoes.text: Ruth said, “Don’t entreat me to leave you, and to return from following after you, for where you go, I will go; and where you lodge, I will lodge; your people shall be my people, and your God my God;
echoes.note: Jesus' covenant formula 'my Father and your Father, my God and your God' (20:17) echoes Ruth's pledge 'your people shall be my people, and your God my God,' a paradigmatic statement of incorporative belonging. Faint verbal contact ('your God / my God') with strong thematic Coherence to adoption.

echoes.text: He will call to me, ‘You are my Father, my God, and the rock of my salvation!’
echoes.note: The royal-messianic 'He will call to me, You are my Father, my God' supplies covenantal background for 'my Father... my God,' linking Jesus' filial claim to the Davidic adoption oracle. Low Volume; one of several candidate Father/God formulae.

harmony.title: The empty tomb
harmony.note: The women come first in all four — but which women, how many angels, and what they did next, each tells differently. The harmony's sharpest divergence is here.

harmony.title: Mary Magdalene meets the risen Lord
harmony.note: "Do not hold on to me." The garden, the spoken name, the first commission — John only.

registers.label: Spare
lines: Early, while it was still dark, she came to the tomb.
And the stone was rolled away.
She wept in the garden, and the gardener spoke her name.
Mary. And she knew the voice of her Lord.
This is the day the Lord has made.
Christ is risen, Alleluia!
Come, let us rejoice and be glad in it.
Christ is risen, Alleluia!

registers.label: Immersive
lines: Come to the garden in the gray of morning, the grass still wet, the tomb standing open and empty.
Christ is risen, Alleluia!
You who came carrying spices for the dead, you who came carrying your grief — look, the stone is rolled away.
Christ is risen, Alleluia!
He stands among the green and growing things and calls you by your name, the way he always has.
Christ is risen, Alleluia!
So run and tell it, you who have seen the Lord: love is stronger than the grave.
Christ is risen, Alleluia!

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: It is dawn in the garden, and the tomb is open.
Christ is risen, Alleluia!
He speaks our name, and grief turns to joy.
Christ is risen, Alleluia!
This is the day the Lord has made.
Christ is risen, Alleluia!
Come, let us worship the living Lord.
We have seen the Lord. Alleluia!
